alternatives: DejaVu Sans appears in a small tutorial subset
candidate_rules.interpretation: Use Arial as the requested face, with sans-serif fallbacks where availability matters.
Large bold axis labels are the most stable cross-repository typographic choice.
Bold 14 pt tick labels recur across recent research, coursework, and tooling.
Titles are bold and usually 18 pt when present; final manuscript figures sometimes suppress them.
Plots explicitly force report-ready white grounds and black text/axes, often to override dark IDE themes.
Retain a complete black box around the axes rather than removing top/right spines.
Inward major ticks matching the 1.8 pt spine width are well supported; length remains context-dependent.
Grid-free final figures are explicit in several independent styles and implicit in many default-reset helpers; absence alone was not counted as explicit evidence.
Legends are normally bold and framed, not frameless.
10 pt is the broadest base candidate, but 11 and 12 pt are credible publication alternatives.
An approximately 4:3, 8 by 6 inch canvas recurs across nine independent repositories.
2 pt is the broadest data-line candidate, while recent sterics figures intentionally use 2.4 pt and spectra often use 2.2 pt.
6 pt is a recurring general marker size; dense XPS and sterics profiles use smaller 4-5.5 pt markers.
Observed values from 0.4 to 1.8 pt correlate with filled, open, and highlighted markers; no honest single default emerges.
Alpha is semantic and artist-specific; lines, components, bars, and diagnostic scatters use different values.
Tight layout is the general finalisation step; constrained layout is a coherent alternative for dense or multi-axis figures.
Recent BO, Ising, and dimer figures use constrained layout for dense compositions.
Tight bounding boxes are nearly universal across the included corpus.

candidate_rules.interpretation: Paired PDF and PNG output is established in PDI and XPS publication workflows; some diagnostics emit only one format.
Both 300 and 600 dpi are established: 600 dominates PDI final figures; 300 dominates XPS, theory-demo, BO, and Gaussian reports.
White, opaque raster output is repeatedly forced for theme-independent reporting.
Dashed neutral reference lines recur broadly; linewidth varies by emphasis.
4 pt caps recur independently, with 2-3 pt compact and 5 pt emphasized alternatives.
Annotations are generally bold and compact; exact size scales with panel density.
This triad is stable across independent PDI calculation and experimental-data repositories; it is not a general-purpose palette.
Explicitly codified in XPS multipanels but not independently established elsewhere.

candidate_rules.candidate_value: quantity or descriptor followed by units in parentheses; math superscripts/subscripts where needed
candidate_rules.interpretation: Units consistently live in parentheses; chemical formulae, inverse powers, and molar exponents use math text, while degree and angstrom symbols are often Unicode.
A global 14 pt default is explicit only in the XPS theme; most other repositories style text roles directly.
Minor ticks are used for quantitative electrochemical axes but deliberately disabled for broad UV-vis/IR spectra; geometry also differs between PDI data and XPS.
PDI experimental helpers retain boxed spines but turn top/right ticks off; the XPS publication theme places inward ticks on visible top/right spines.
